blogs.title: Stopping Yourself in Words: Why LLMs Should Think in Patches, Not Tokens
blogs.description: Most large language models waste massive amounts of compute by processing every single token with the same intensity, regardless of whether it's predicting 'the' or complex code. This post explains BLT's 'entropy patching' technique, which dynamically groups bytes into 'patches' based on prediction difficulty. We'll visualize how this allows the model to skip easy sections (saving energy) and focus heavy computation only where data gets complex.

blogs.title: The 50% Energy Saver: How Tokenizer-Free Models Beat Big Competition
blogs.description: Can we get the smarts of a 13B model with the speed of a 7B model? Not necessarily, but we can match them with fewer compute operations (flops). This article breaks down BLT's 'flop-controlled scaling' studies, showing how variable patch sizes allow models to trade inference steps for model depth. We compare BLT's efficiency directly against Llama 3 to demonstrate how significantly reducing unnecessary calculations leads to real-world cost savings.

blogs.title: Seeing the Letters: Why Byte-Level Models Are Better at Coding and Reasoning
blogs.description: When you strip away the standard vocabulary that turns text into abstract symbols, you lose some information—but only if you throw it away. Here, we explore why training directly on raw bytes gives models a superpower: character-level robustness. Through examples of noisy inputs, low-resource languages, and understanding phonology, we show that by keeping track of individual bytes, BLT models can dodge errors that confuse standard tokenizers.

blogs.title: Breaking the Token Ceiling: A New Architectural Frontier for AI Scaling
blogs.description: Traditional AI scaling hits a wall where making models bigger slows them down because indices and vocabuaries don't scale gracefully. This post introduces the insight from 'Patches Scale Better Than Tokens.' We explain how decoupling model size from vocabulary constraints lets researchers simultaneously grow the network's intelligence and its processing chunks without breaking stride or inflation costs.
